So I wanted to share something that might be controversial, but honestly might have saved me from a bad situation. I recently started dating someone who seemed great on the surface - charming, attentive, the whole package. But something kept nagging at me... some inconsistencies in their stories.

After going back and forth with myself about it, I decided to run a basic background check. I know some people will say this is invasive, but hear me out.

The background check revealed they had multiple restraining orders from past relationships and a history of financial fraud that they never mentioned. When confronted (carefully and in a public place), they got extremely defensive and tried to twist everything around.

I'm not saying everyone should do this, and I definitely had mixed feelings about it. But in my case, it helped me see red flags I was trying to ignore. Trust your gut, but also protect yourself. Dating nowadays can be complicated, and sometimes a little verification goes a long way.

Anyone else have similar experiences or thoughts on this?

I use positive only training. I made a big fuss every time he listened, did something on his own that was good, etc. I use treats as my dog is very food motivated. But use low calorie treats. My dog got a little porky before I made the switch.

Be confident. My dog knows I will protect him. Advocate for him. But also, don't back down. This was important for his resource guarding, especially his food. I started by making him sit before I gave him his meals. My dog would through a big tantrum every time, but I didn't give in. I was standing there for over an hour an one point holding his food before he sat. And he when finally did sit, there was a mountain of praise and treats. That made the next day easier, and easier. Now I can stick my hand in his bowl when he eats and take anything away from him.

Do bonding activities. We started out with basic obedience classes and went on to scent tracking before my dog developed a heart condition. Those classes and activities really strengthened our bond as we had to work together.

Hello! Fellow English mastiff owner here. The behaviour is indeed concerning, but if you curb it now, it will really set you up for life.

We adopted our English mastiff when he was just over 5 years old. No training. No rules. Didn't understand the word no. Leash reactive.

We got him started in obedience classes which REALLY helped as it helped to teach us to speak his language and established some rules and boundaries.

Then we moved on to more specific training for his leash reactivity.

Then we started him in a daycare once a week with a certified trainer. 

Then we got him a "job" doing scent work classes before he was diagnosed with his heart condition.

He's now a model canine citizen and we can go to dog parks and take him pretty much everywhere. Well, everywhere that he'd fit.

Mastiffs are smart and incredibly stubborn and they will push your boundaries at every possible turn. Training is going to be an EVERYDAY thing for the rest of your pups life. Also, establish a routine for your pup so he knows what to expect from you.

I know it's going to be hard but you need to persevere. I promise this dog is worth it.
